title: Pricing
intro: We are paid for outcomes we can measure against a holdout, not for minutes we can inflate.

sections.heading: Pilot
sections.body: An eight-week pilot on India-originating bookings: payment rescue and booking confirmation, with a no-call holdout to measure lift.
points: Fixed fee [[spec:offer.pilot_fee|USD 20,000]], with [[spec:offer.pilot_at_risk|half]] at risk against the agreed success metrics.
Containment target [[spec:offer.containment_target|35 to 55 percent]]. A target, not a measured result.

sections.heading: After the pilot
sections.body: Two options. Pick the one whose unit you trust more.
points: Per outcome: [[spec:offer.retainer|USD 6,000 a month]] plus [[spec:offer.per_resolved|Rs 25 per contact the AI resolves]] with no human.

sections.heading: Why per outcome
sections.body: A per-minute price rewards long calls. A per-resolved-contact price rewards short calls that finish the job, which is what a customer wants too. Resolved means the journey's goal was met on the call (payment link accepted, or details confirmed) with no human involved.

sections.heading: What a call costs to run
sections.body: Our unit economics page lists each cost component (telephony, speech, model, voice, WhatsApp, infrastructure) with its unit price, source and the date it was checked. Prices are re-checked before any quote.
points: Text-to-speech list price [[S-31|Rs 3.00 per 1,000 characters]] (Sarvam Bulbul v3).
WhatsApp utility template [[S-30|Rs 0.1150 plus 18% GST]] (Meta, India).

sections.heading: Enterprise path
sections.body: Run as a managed service first. When you are ready, the same Helm chart runs on your Kubernetes and we hand it over: build, operate, transfer. Private deployment, SSO, data residency and an SLA are part of the enterprise agreement.
